Hi Andreia, this is Mark Daniels from SimSurg. Thank you for meeting me at the congress in Orlando. As promised, here is a quick summary of our offer. Our training bundle includes the simulator, the software and forty hours of hands-on training for your nursing team. The full price is forty-two thousand dollars. I can offer you a ten percent discount, as long as you sign the contract before the end of the month. We also offer a free thirty-day trial period, so your nurses can test the simulator first. And the warranty covers two years, provided that our technicians do the maintenance. I will send you the written quote by email today. Please call me if you have any questions.

Hi Claudia, it's Andreia. I just finished the call with Mark from SimSurg, and I have good news. First, they agreed to split the payment. We pay thirty percent upfront and the rest in six monthly installments. Second, they will extend the warranty to three years, on condition that we sign a maintenance contract. They did not accept a bigger discount, so we met halfway. The discount stays at ten percent, but they will add twenty extra hours of training for free. I think it is a win-win deal, and very cost-effective for our team. Unless you see a problem, I will tell Mark that we are ready to sign on Friday. Talk soon.

Here is how Andreia negotiates with the supplier. First, she listens to the sales pitch and asks for a written quote. Then she compares the price of the bundle with other suppliers. Next, she asks for a free trial period for her team. After that, she sets her conditions: a longer warranty and payment in installments. Finally, they meet halfway and agree on a win-win deal.
